output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise in lost bags comes from Corvane's tag labels failing to scan automatically, not from the handler. Tags printed on the new Fennick stock since 1 Sep fail to read about 11.8% of the time, against about 1.5% before. Corvane's transfer tags and Pelion's tags are unaffected. Failed bags go to the manual encode desk, where waits rose from 7 to about 30 minutes, and 91% of the missed bags reached the lateral after it closed. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crews and its rate stayed flat. That argues strongly against a crew problem. On 14–16 Oct, counters using old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12.1%. Next steps: switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock held in stores (valid contract to 31 Dec). Separately, test whether the fault lies in the Fennick media or in the printer heat setting. Hold any defect claim against Fennick until that test is done. Ask HBAA for a temporary extra encode workstation in the evening bank. I'm fairly confident in this. The open question is media versus printer settings, and that doesn't change the first step.
output.methodChoice: Origin network and propagation tracing, with discriminating evidence (tag-read telemetry by tag range; reconciliation by routing path and carrier)
